anatomy.intro: Spines sit at the tubercle tips, while flowers emerge from the spaces between these raised green mounds.

parts.function: Each projecting green mound is part of the succulent, photosynthetic stem.
parts.label: Tubercle

parts.function: The cushion at a tubercle's tip bears its spine cluster.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: Shorter outward-spreading spines form a protective star around the areole.
parts.label: Radial spines

parts.function: The stronger spine projects beyond the radial spokes.
parts.label: Central spine

flowers.text: Tiny cream, pale green, or yellowish flowers nestle between tubercles. The conspicuous red club-shaped projection recorded on this plant is a fruit from an earlier bloom.

growth.note: Look closely at the tubercles: their intersecting spiral rows organize the body, with flowers appearing in the spaces between them.

stages.text: The green body is organized into spirals of tubercles.
stages.title: Rounded juvenile

stages.text: Established stems become larger globes or short cylinders.
stages.title: Broadening body

stages.text: Small pale flowers can be followed by conspicuous red club-shaped fruits.
stages.title: Flower and fruit

habitat.text: Mammillaria mammillaris occurs in the southern Caribbean and northern South America, including northeastern Colombia and northern Venezuela. It grows in seasonally dry tropical vegetation.

No flowers, grafts, or roots. Numbers must remain readable at 350px. Generic anatomical specimen, not measurement evidence. A Mammillaria mammillaris cactus: one rounded short cylinder, green prominent conical tubercles arranged in spirals, white wool in the gaps near the crown, sparse straight tan/dark central spines and shorter pale radial spines. Exactly 1 points to a green conical tubercle, 2 to a small spine-bearing areole at its tip, 3 to short pale radial spines, 4 to one long straight dark central spine. No red fruit.

lookalikes.name: Probable Mammillaria rekoi
lookalikes.text: The rekoi candidate has finer, denser pale radial spines and conspicuous hooked central spines; this plant's larger exposed tubercles and pale flowers support a different ID.

mature.text: Rounded to short-cylindrical stems reach about 8–20 cm across, growing alone or sometimes in clumps.

milestones.text: Purchased at Carlsons' Greenhouse in a 4-inch pot.
milestones.title: Joined the collection

milestones.text: Close photographs showed large tubercles, dark-tipped spines, tiny cream flowers or buds, and a red club-shaped fruit.
milestones.title: Identification observations

nameStory.text: Linnaeus published Cactus mammillaris in 1753; Kew dates the present Mammillaria combination to 1886.
